1  NO.314/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER,
 MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, GANGAVATHI, PARTLY  ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING  ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11436  MFA No. 100577 of 2018  ORAL JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by the injured-claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment & award dated 15.11.2017 passed in MVC No.314/2016 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & MACT., Gangavathi (for short, 'Tribunal').
3. Heard.
4.

Learned counsel Smt.Sitalaxmi Purli appearing for the appellant-claimant would submit that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing income, disability of the claimant and further submits that the award of compensation on all other heads is also on the lower side.
Hence, she seeks for reassessment of the compensation amount appropriately by allowing the appeal.

Per contra, learned counsel Sri.M.Y.Katagi appearing for respondent No.3/Insurance Company supporting the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal submits that in the absence of cogent and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month, which is just and proper and needs no interference.
He further submits that award of compensation by the Tribunal on all heads is just and proper, does not call for interference.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
6. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the appeal papers along with material available on record.
7. The evidence available on record indicates that the appellant-claimant sustained grievous injuries in a road accident dated 04.01.2016.
The appellant sustained fracture of tibia and fibula.
PW2 in his evidence has deposed that the appellant has sustained 22% to 24% disability to whole body.
Considering the same, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 8%.
This Court taking note of the oral testimony of the PW2 and Wound Certificate at Ex.P6 and other medical evidence NC:

Sri. Raja @ Raju S/O Kotrayya @ Kotresh vs Abdul S/O Rajasab on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99677860/
2 2024:KHC-D:11436 available on record, is of the considered view that it would be just and proper to re-assess the disability at 12%.

sentences.text: Similarly, the income of the appellant is reassessed notionally at Rs.8,750/- per month placing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Admittedly, the appellant has provided treatment and was inpatient for a period of 20 days.
8. There is no dispute with regard to the age of the injured as 37 years and multiplier of 15.

Thus,
loss of future income due to disability is recomputed as under:
Rs.8,750 (income) x 12(months) x 15(multiplier) x 12% (disability) = Rs.1,89,000/-
9.

In view of the above, this Court reassesses the compensation as under:
 HEADS AMOUNT  (in Rs.)
Loss of future earnings due to disability 1,89,000/-
Towards pain and suffering 40,000/-
Loss of amenities 30,000/-
Loss of earning during treatment 26,250/-
(i.e.Rs.8,750 X 3 months)
Diet, nourishment, conveyance and 20,000/-
attendant charges  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11436 Towards Medical expenses 36,535/-
 Total 3,41,785/-
10.
Thus, the claimant shall be entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,41,785/- as against Rs.1,70,935/- awarded by the learned Tribunal.

11. In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,41,785/- as against Rs.1,70,935/- awarded by the Tribunal.

c) The compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
d) The Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today.
e) On such deposit, the same shall be released in favour of the appellant/claimant.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11436 f) Registry to transmit the records, if any, forthwith to the Tribunal.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.
